sections.h2: Capacity must grow from 220 Mt to 604 Mt, close to the recent pace

chart.title: The draft's 604 Mt capacity target is 2.7 times today's 220 Mt
chart.sub: Crude steel capacity, million tonnes a year.
chart.source: JPC and Ministry of Steel; 2017 policy; draft policy (Oct 2026).

sections.means: Capacity rose by about 20 Mt a year over the last three years, and the draft's 2047 target needs about 18 Mt a year.
sections.todo: Watch capacity utilisation, which slipped to about 77% in 2025-26 as capacity grew faster than output.

sections.h2: Blast furnaces keep a large share of 2047 steel on the draft's coal figure

chart.title: Blast furnaces would still make 229 to 303 Mt of 2047 steel
chart.sub: Blast-furnace crude steel in 2047, Mt, implied by the draft's coking-coal forecast.
chart.source: Draft policy; World Steel Association; this blog's arithmetic.
ref: 529 Mt, total crude steel needed in 2047

sections.means: The draft's 236 Mt of coking coal supports 229 to 303 Mt of blast-furnace steel, or 43 to 57% of the 529 Mt needed.
sections.todo: Plan for coking coal imports rising to about 3.3 times today's level, through long-term contracts and domestic mining.

sections.h2: Blast-furnace emissions must fall about 35% for the 1.54 t goal

chart.title: Blast furnaces would need to fall to 1.66-1.68 t CO2 a tonne
chart.sub: CO2 per tonne of crude steel from blast furnaces, t.
chart.source: This blog's arithmetic; BigMint ranges for India; draft policy.
ref: 1.54 t, the industry average the draft targets

sections.means: Even with all other steel gas- or scrap-based, blast furnaces would have to emit 1.66 to 1.68 t against 2.5 to 2.7 t today.
sections.todo: Fund carbon capture, hydrogen or gas injection, or biomass for blast furnaces, none of which is yet in commercial use at scale in India.
